draft.title: The electrochemical series
card: The electrochemical series lists reduction half-equations in order of their standard electrode potentials, E°, measured in volts. The most positive E° is at the top, where the strongest oxidising agents are found.

A species on the left of a half-equation is an oxidising agent. The higher its E°, the stronger it is. The species on the right is a reducing agent, and it is stronger the lower the E° of its half-equation.

To predict a reaction, pair the oxidising agent with the higher E° (it is reduced) with the reducing agent from the half-equation with the lower E° (it is oxidised). A reaction predicted this way is spontaneous under standard conditions.
Cell voltage = E° of the reduction half-equation minus E° of the oxidation half-equation, both taken as written in the table. A positive answer means the reaction is predicted to occur.
draft.remember: The higher half-equation is reduced, the lower one is reversed. Voltage = E° (reduced) minus E° (oxidised).

a.q: Which statement about the electrochemical series is correct?
opts: The oxidising agent on the higher half-equation is stronger
The reducing agent on the higher half-equation is stronger
Lower E° values belong to the stronger oxidising agents
Half-equations are ordered by the number of electrons
a.why: A more positive E° means the species on the left is better at gaining electrons, so it is a stronger oxidising agent. The reducing agent is stronger when its half-equation has a lower E°, so the second option is the reverse.
a.clue: Think about which end of the table has the strongest oxidising agents.

b.q: Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ ⇌ Cu(s) has E° = +0.34 V. Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ ⇌ Zn(s) has E° = -0.76 V. What is predicted for a standard cell made from these two half-cells?
opts: Zn is oxidised, and the cell voltage is 1.10 V
Cu is oxidised, and the cell voltage is 1.10 V
Zn is oxidised, and the cell voltage is 0.42 V
Cu is oxidised, and the cell voltage is 0.42 V
b.why: Cu²⁺ has the higher E°, so it is reduced and Zn is oxidised. Voltage = +0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10 V. Subtracting gives the wrong size when the signs are ignored, which is how 0.42 V arises.
b.clue: Subtract the lower E° from the higher, keeping the negative sign.

a.best: The oxidising agent on the higher half-equation is stronger

b.best: Zn is oxidised, and the cell voltage is 1.10 V

check.summary: No problems found. The card matches the VCE data book convention (highest E° at the top), and both questions have a single clearly correct answer.
